paper_metadata.title: Association of COVID-19 with Intracranial Hemorrhage during Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A 10-Year Retrospective Observational Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the setting well. However, the sample is highly selected (only those who received a cCT), which likely overestimates the incidence of the outcome (ICRH) compared to the general ECMO population, though the authors acknowledge this.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were included if they had received a cranial computed tomography (cCT) scan during vv-ECMO support or within 72 h after ECMO removal. Additional inclusion criteria were ages of at least 18 years and vv-ECMO support of at least 6 h.
items.reasoning: Criteria are explicit, including the 'zero time' (ECMO initiation).

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Cerebral CT scans during or immediately after ECMO treatment were available from 618 patients (51.3%). Of these, 204 patients (16.9%) were treated with high-flow vv-ECMO systems for ARDS and were included for further analyses
items.reasoning: Only 51.3% of the total ECMO population had imaging. Since imaging was likely triggered by clinical suspicion, this introduces selection bias regarding the prognostic factor's relationship with the outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome was defined by objective imaging (CT) and reviewed by multiple blinded experts, which is a high-quality approach.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Cranial CT scans were visually assessed for the presence of intraparenchymal hemorrhage, intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), subarachnoid hemorrhage, and subdural or epidural hematoma. For the purpose of statistical analyses, all types of hemorrhage were summarized as ICRH.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined and categorized.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: All CT data were reviewed independently by one neurosurgeon (TP) and one neurointensivist (MF), who were blinded for the patients' diagnoses including the presence of acute brain injury. When these two did not concur, cranial CT scans were reviewed by another experienced neurosurgeon (PC).
items.reasoning: Blinded independent review by specialists with a tie-breaker is a robust method.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement

items.evidence_snippet: Computed tomography scan evaluation was performed with Centricity Universal Viewer Zero Footprint Client®
items.reasoning: Standardized imaging and software were used for all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While multivariable Cox regression was used, the 10-year span introduces significant temporal confounding (changes in ARDS/ECMO care), which the authors tried to adjust for by 'year of implantation', but residual confounding remains likely.
